title: Adapt Human Motion for Robots with NVIDIA SOMA Retargeter | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: NVIDIA describes its open-source SOMA Retargeter, which adapts human motion on the shared SOMA skeleton to specific humanoid robots via scaling, Newton/Warp inverse kinematics and foot-plant correction, outputting CSV joint trajectories for policy training (SONIC, ProtoMotions). The v0.2 release ships configurations for five humanoids (Unitree G1/H2, Booster T1, AgiBot X2 Ultra, AgiBot A3T3), positioning NVIDIA as the data-pipeline layer for humanoid training.

themes.theme: Why human motion must be retargeted

insights.claim: Human demonstrations capture the coordination and timing of natural movement, but robots cannot copy human joint motion directly because their proportions, joint structure and range of motion differ.
insights.speaker: John Malaska
insights.so_what: Retargeting is a necessary data-pipeline step for humanoid learning, a tooling layer NVIDIA is moving to own.
insights.quote: a robot cannot simply copy the same joint motion from a human

insights.claim: Human motion sources such as mocap, video, datasets and generative models output different skeletons and file formats, and representing them on the shared SOMA skeleton (from NVIDIA SOMA-X) gives the retargeter a consistent input.
insights.speaker: John Malaska
insights.so_what: A common skeleton standard is a platform play: whoever defines the representation anchors the ecosystem.
insights.locator: Human motion can come from many sources

insights.claim: SOMA Retargeter reads BVH animation on the SOMA base skeleton, scales motion targets to the robot, solves joint poses with inverse kinematics, applies corrections, and outputs a CSV of per-frame root position, orientation and joint angles.
insights.speaker: John Malaska
insights.so_what: Standardized, open outputs make NVIDIA tooling easy to slot into robotics developers' training stacks.
insights.locator: SOMA Retargeter reads a Biovision Hierarchy

insights.claim: The retargeting solver uses inverse kinematics from Newton, built with NVIDIA Warp, with IK weights deciding which body parts take priority when a robot cannot match every target.
insights.speaker: John Malaska
insights.so_what: Pulls developers onto NVIDIA's simulation/physics software stack (Newton, Warp).
insights.locator: The retargeting solver uses inverse kinematics

insights.claim: An experimental IK weight optimizer tunes weights by retargeting a small set of task-representative motions and scoring how closely and smoothly the robot follows targets.
insights.speaker: John Malaska
insights.so_what: Automated tuning lowers the labor cost of onboarding new robot embodiments.

insights.claim: Sliding feet create conflicting targets for a motion-tracking policy, so foot-plant correction adjusts foot motion during detected contact intervals before data enters training.
insights.speaker: John Malaska
insights.so_what: Data quality artifacts directly affect policy training outcomes; cleaning tools add value to the pipeline.
insights.quote: Sliding feet can introduce conflicting targets for a downstream motion-tracking policy

insights.claim: The Robot Configurator aligns human and robot reference poses and maps skeletons; in a Booster T1 example, an unaligned reference pose turned a one-handed wave into both arms held outward.
insights.speaker: John Malaska
insights.so_what: Shows configuration quality is decisive for usable robot motion data.

themes.theme: Ecosystem of motion data and robot embodiments

insights.claim: The SOMA Retargeter v0.2 release includes BONES-SEED sample motions supplied by Bones and reference configurations for five humanoids: Unitree G1, Unitree H2, Booster T1, AgiBot X2 Ultra and AgiBot A3T3.
insights.speaker: John Malaska
insights.so_what: Maps the humanoid OEMs (largely Chinese) aligning with NVIDIA's robotics software stack.

insights.claim: Human motion for retargeting can come from BONES-SEED mocap data, GEM-X single-video 3D reconstruction, or the Kimodo and ARDY generative models that produce motion on the SOMA skeleton from text and pose constraints.
insights.speaker: John Malaska
insights.so_what: Generative and video-derived motion could scale humanoid training data beyond costly mocap capture.

themes.theme: From retargeted motion to trained policies

insights.claim: Retargeted CSV trajectories convert into motion-library formats for policy training in SONIC (which includes a SOMA CSV converter for G1) or ProtoMotions, followed by simulation evaluation of balance, ground contact, actuator limits and tracking accuracy.
insights.speaker: John Malaska
insights.so_what: End-to-end NVIDIA pipeline from human data to sim-validated robot policy deepens platform lock-in.

insights.claim: In a separate experiment, Bones human motion was adapted for the MicroDuck robot and used to train per-clip controllers in physics simulation with Isaac Lab and Newton.
insights.speaker: John Malaska
insights.so_what: Demonstrates the pipeline generalizes beyond humanoids to small hobby robots.
insights.locator: In a separate experiment with MicroDuck

insights.claim: The MotionBricks G1 model, trained partly on BONES-SEED motions retargeted with SOMA Retargeter, generates continuous whole-body G1 motion between changing target poses in real time and has been demonstrated on a physical Unitree G1 with SONIC executing it.
insights.speaker: John Malaska
insights.so_what: Shows retargeted data feeding generative motion models that run on real hardware, a step toward deployable humanoid behaviors.
